sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: DEEP UPPER TROUGH IN THE WEST IS FORECAST TO LIFT NEWD TOWARD THE NRN ROCKIES/NRN PLAINS AS STRONG SHORTWAVE TROUGH...MOVING THROUGH NV EARLY THIS MORNING...SHIFTS INTO ERN MT BY LATE AFTERNOON. THIS WILL RESULT IN AN EWD MOVING COLD FRONT TO STRETCH FROM WRN ND SWWD INTO FAR WRN NEB BY 00Z. THE UPPER TROUGH AND COLD FRONT...PLUS A WARM FRONT STRETCHING FROM NERN MO NWWD INTO ND SHOULD PROVIDE PRIMARY FOCUS FOR SEVERE WEATHER FROM THE NRN PLAINS SEWD INTO THE LOWER MO RIVER VALLEY. ALSO...AN UPPER TROUGH MOVING THROUGH NEW ENGLAND WILL HELP PUSH A WEAK COLD FRONT SWD INTO THE CAROLINAS AND SRN APPALACHIANS AND ENHANCE THUNDERSTORMS IN THIS REGION.

sections.title: NRN PLAINS SEWD INTO THE LOWER MO RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: CONVECTION IS LIKELY TO BE ONGOING AT THE START OF THE PERIOD ACROSS IA WITHIN ZONE OF WARM ADVECTION. WHILE CONVECTION SHOULD WEAKEN DURING THE MORNING AS LOW LEVEL JET BACKS ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS...REMNANT CLOUDS AND RAIN-COOLED AIR SHOULD REINFORCE WARM FRONT. THOUGH STRONG DYNAMICAL FORCING IS NOT EXPECTED...DIFFERENTIAL HEATING NEAR THE FRONT IS EXPECTED TO PROVIDE SUFFICIENT LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE FOR CONVECTIVE INITIATION ACROSS THE LOWER MO RIVER VALLEY LATE AFTERNOON. IN THE NRN PLAINS...APPROACHING SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND EWD MOVING COLD FRONT SHOULD PROVIDE A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR THUNDERSTORMS. STRONGLY WARMING TEMPERATURES OF MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER...DEWPOINTS IN THE 70S...BETWEEN COLD FRONT AND WARM FRONT WILL RESULT IN MLCAPES TO RANGE FROM 3000 TO 4000 J/KG. STRONG WIND FIELDS ACROSS THE DAKOTAS AND VEERING WIND PROFILES ELSEWHERE ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA WILL PROVIDE FAVORABLE VERTICAL SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS. BACKED LOW LEVEL WINDS AND THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY SUGGEST A FEW TORNADOES ARE POSSIBLE. HOWEVER...THE MAIN THREAT SHOULD BE VERY LARGE HAIL AND STRONG TO SEVERE DOWNDRAFTS. THE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD DIMINISH BETWEEN 03Z-06Z AS STORMS SHIFT EWD INTO A MORE

sections.title: SRN APPALACHIANS REGION
sections.text: ALTHOUGH THE SRN EXTENSION OF STRONGER WINDS ALOFT ASSOCIATED WITH NEW ENGLAND TROUGH WILL REMAIN NORTH OF AREA...THE COMBINATION OF STRONG HEATING...A VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS/MLCAPES IN EXCESS OF 3000 J/KG/ AND THE PRESENCE OF A WEAK FRONT ALONG HIGHER TERRAIN SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR AFTERNOON THUNDERSTORMS. ALTHOUGH DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL ONLY BE IN THE 10-20 KT RANGE... THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY COMBINED WITH STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES...25F TEMPERATURE/DEWPOINTS SPREADS...SUGGEST THAT WIND DAMAGE WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STORMS AS THEY MOVE FROM NORTHEAST TO SOUTHWEST. SINCE STORMS WILL BE THERMODYNAMICALLY DRIVEN...THEY SHOULD WEAKEN QUICKLY AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: ERN NM AREA
sections.text: STORMS ARE ONCE AGAIN LIKELY TO DEVELOP WITHIN PLUME OF MOIST MID/HIGH LEVEL MOISTURE FLOWING IN FROM THE SOUTHWEST. DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELL STORMS AND DEEP MIXED LAYER TO 600 MB MAY ALSO SUPPORT A FEW STRONG/SEVERE WIND GUST DURING THE LATER AFTERNOON/EVENING HOURS. ..IMY/COHEN.. 06/02/2011

sections.title: NRN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: AN EMBEDDED MID-UPPER LEVEL SPEED MAX OVER UT THIS MORNING WILL EJECT NEWD TO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS BY THIS EVENING/EARLY TONIGHT...WHILE AN ASSOCIATED SURFACE CYCLONE OVER ERN MT MOVES NWD TO SRN SASKATCHEWAN AND DEEPENS. SE OF THE LOW...A COLD FRONT WILL PROGRESS EWD INTO THE DAKOTAS THIS EVENING/TONIGHT...WHILE A WARM FRONT MOVES NWD INTO THE ERN DAKOTAS. A RELATIVELY WARM EML WILL ACT TO CAP THE WARM SECTOR THROUGH MUCH OF THE DAY ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS. INITIAL STORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED BY MID AFTERNOON ACROSS NE MT IN PROXIMITY TO THE SURFACE LOW ON THE NW EDGE OF THE UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR...WHILE STORM DEVELOPMENT FARTHER TO THE E/SE WILL LIKELY BE DELAYED UNTIL THIS EVENING. SURFACE HEATING/MIXING AND ASCENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT/REMNANT LEE TROUGH SHOULD SUPPORT SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT BY ABOUT 00Z ACROSS CENTRAL NEB/DAKOTAS...AND THIS CONVECTION WILL SPREAD NEWD TOWARD THE ERN DAKOTAS EARLY TONIGHT. THE INITIAL CONVECTION WILL BE IN AN ENVIRONMENT WITH LARGELY UNIDIRECTIONAL DEEP-LAYER SHEAR AND MLCAPE OF 2500-3000 J/KG...WHICH WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. EARLY OVERNIGHT...THE CONVECTION WILL LIKELY EVOLVE

sections.title: NE MO AREA TODAY
sections.text: A REMNANT MCV IS MOVING EWD OVER NW MO...WHILE OTHER CONVECTION OVER NE MO/W CENTRAL IL IS REINFORCING THE SURFACE WARM FRONT. WIDESPREAD DEBRIS CLOUDINESS FROM THE OVERNIGHT CONVECTION CASTS SOME DOUBT ON THE DEGREE OF SURFACE HEATING/DESTABILIZATION IN ADVANCE OF THE MCV AND ALONG THE WARM FRONT/OUTFLOW IN NE MO LATER TODAY. STILL...THERE WILL BE A NARROW WINDOW OF OPPORTUNITY THIS AFTERNOON FOR RENEWED DEVELOPMENT WITH THE MCV ALONG THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY...WHERE MODERATE INSTABILITY AND SUFFICIENT DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL BE PRESENT FOR SUPERCELLS. ASSUMING NEW SURFACE-BASED STORMS FORM THIS AFTERNOON...ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE BEFORE THE CAP STRENGTHENS LATER THIS EVENING.

sections.title: SC PIEDMONT AND N GA AREA THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: THE MID-UPPER LEVEL RIDGE IS ESTABLISHED OVER THE MID SOUTH AND SRN APPALACHIANS THIS MORNING. THE MCV OVER NRN MO IS THE ONLY IDENTIFIABLE UPSTREAM SYSTEM...AND THAT WILL NOT REACH THE SRN APPALACHIANS UNTIL LATE TONIGHT IN A WEAKENED STATE. THUS...THE ONLY FACTORS FAVORING STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON ARE STRONG DAYTIME HEATING AND WEAK ASCENT ALONG A STALLED FRONT. THE COMBINATION OF AFTERNOON MLCAPE OF 2000-3000 J/KG...SURFACE TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS OF 25-30 F...AND ONLY WEAK NLY SHEAR ALOFT COULD SUPPORT ISOLATED STRONG DOWNBURSTS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL. STORM COVERAGE AND INTENSITY WILL BE ON THE LOWER MARGINS TO JUSTIFY A SLIGHT RISK.

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: DEEP MIXING ALONG THE LEE TROUGH WILL RESULT IN INVERTED-V PROFILES AND THE POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED HIGH-BASED THUNDERSTORMS WITH STRONG DOWNBURSTS LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. ..THOMPSON/GARNER.. 06/02/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER PARTS OF MO/IL
sections.text: BROAD CYCLONIC FLOW OVER THE WESTERN STATES THIS MORNING WILL MAINTAIN A BAND OF MODERATELY STRONG MID LEVEL WINDS FROM AZ/NM INTO THE NORTHERN PLAINS. A RELATIVELY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AIR MASS IS IN PLACE OVER MOST OF THE PLAINS THIS MORNING WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S AND 60S FROM ND SOUTHWARD. MORNING SOUNDINGS SUGGEST A STRONG CAPPING INVERSION IS IN PLACE IN MOST AREAS...WHICH WILL PRECLUDE DEEP CONVECTION UNTIL LATE AFTERNOON AND EVENING.

sections.title: SOUTHERN/CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: MODELS SUGGEST A FEW INTENSE THUNDERSTORMS WILL FIRST FORM OVER EASTERN NM...THEN NORTHWARD INTO PARTS OF CO/KS. STORM COVERAGE APPEARS TO BE LOW...BUT SUFFICIENTLY STRONG SOUTHWEST FLOW ALOFT AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL PROMOTE A RISK OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. THE RISK AREA IN THE SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS SHOULD BE RELATIVELY NARROW WITH ACTIVITY WEAKENING BY MID EVENING.

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: MORE ORGANIZED STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP OVER WESTERN NEB/SD BY EARLY EVENING AND SPREAD NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA. SOME OF THE MESOSCALE MODELS ALSO SUGGEST DISCRETE DEVELOPMENT MAY OCCUR OVER CENTRAL ND DURING THE EVENING AS THE LOW LEVEL JET STRENGTHENS. RATHER STRONG VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE PRESENT IN THIS REGION...PROMOTING SUPERCELL STORMS CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: MO/IL
sections.text: A PERSISTENT MCS REMAINS OVER IA/MO/IL THIS MORNING...WITH WIDESPREAD CLOUDS ON THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF THE SYSTEM. THOSE CLOUDS ARE EXPECTED TO DIMINISH THROUGH THE AFTERNOON...RESULTING IN RATHER STRONG HEATING OVER PARTS OF EASTERN MO AND CENTRAL/SOUTHERN IL. THE REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM THE SYSTEM MAY PROVIDE A FOCUS FOR REDEVELOPMENT OF THUNDERSTORMS LATER TODAY ALONG THE MS RIVER. IF STORMS CAN FORM...ENVIRONMENT WOULD SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELL OR SUPERCELL STORMS CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST STATES
sections.text: IT STILL APPEARS LIKELY THAT A FEW INTENSE THUNDERSTORMS WILL DEVELOP OVER THE MOUNTAINS OF GA/SC THIS AFTERNOON...BENEATH THE UPPER RIDGE. LATEST MODEL SOLUTIONS SUGGEST THE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE RATHER LOW COVERAGE. FOR THIS REASON...HAVE OPTED TO REMOVE THE SLIGHT RISK FOR THIS REGION. NEVERTHELESS...THOSE STORMS THAT DO FORM WILL BE IN AN ENVIRONMENT OF AMPLE MOISTURE AND HIGH CAPE...FAVORABLE FOR WET MICROBURSTS OR HAIL. ..HART/JIRAK.. 06/02/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS MAINLY THE DAKOTAS
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS IN SC...

sections.title: SD/ND AREA
sections.text: CONVECTION HAD GRADUALLY INCREASED IN COVERAGE ACROSS FAR NWRN NEB AND SWRN SD THE PAST COUPLE OF HOURS...POSSIBLY IN RESPONSE TO A WEAK SHORTWAVE TROUGH LIFTING NEWD FROM NERN CO. OPERATIONAL AND HIGH RESOLUTION STORM SCALE MODELS ARE ALL IN AGREEMENT OF THIS CONVECTION GROWING UPSCALE...ESPECIALLY AS IT MOVES EAST OF THE SURFACE TROUGH IN FAR WRN NEB/SD/ND AND ENCOUNTERS A MUCH MOISTER BOUNDARY LAYER. THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AND STEEPENING LAPSE RATES...SEE RAP 00Z SOUNDING...WERE RESULTING IN MLCAPES FROM 2500-4000 J/KG. DEEP LAYER SHEAR...CURRENTLY AT 30-50 KT...WILL INCREASE DURING THE NIGHT AS 60-70 KT MID LEVEL JET MAX SPREADS EWD FROM THE ROCKIES AND LOW LEVEL JET INCREASES TO BETWEEN 50-70 KT. ALTHOUGH THE INSTABILITY WILL WEAKEN SOMEWHAT THROUGH THE NIGHT AS THE SURFACE TEMPERATURES COOL...THE SHEAR AND INSTABILITY/STEEP LAPSE RATES SHOULD BE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS WITH MAINLY A SEVERE HAIL AND WIND THREAT...REFERENCE WW 421.

sections.title: SC
sections.text: A CLUSTER OF SEVERE STORMS DEVELOPED OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WRN NC AND HAVE BEEN MOVING SSEWD AT 25 KT. ALTHOUGH THE DEEP LAYER SHEAR WERE ONLY IN THE 20-30 KT RANGE...NLY WINDS ABOVE THE BOUNDARY LAYER WERE MOVING THE STORMS SSEWD AT 25 KT...WITH RELATIVELY STRONG SR INFLOW. THE WARM AND MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER COUPLED WITH MLCAPES FROM 3000-4000 J/KG WILL LIKELY SUPPORT A SEVERE THREAT WITH THESE STORMS THE NEXT 2-3 HOURS...WHEN THEY SHOULD WEAKEN AS SURFACE TEMPERATURES COOL.

sections.title: WRN TX/ERN NM NEWD INTO SWRN KS
sections.text: NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS WERE LOCATED ACROSS THIS AREA WITHIN PLUME OF MID/HIGH LEVEL TROPICAL MOISTURE. THE DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS NOT PARTICULARLY STRONG...BUT TEMPERATURE/DEWPOINT SPREADS BETWEEN 40 AND 50 DEGREES IMMEDIATELY ON THE EAST END OF THE CONVECTION CERTAINLY COULD RESULT IN STRONG GUSTY WINDS...WITH A FEW GUSTS POSSIBLY REACHING SEVERE CRITERIA FOR A BRIEF PERIOD OF TIME. THE BOUNDARY LAYER SHOULD COOL SUFFICIENTLY BY 03Z TO DIMINISH THE HIGHER CONVECTIVE WIND THREAT THEREAFTER.

sections.title: MO
sections.text: STORMS THAT DEVELOPED EARLIER OVER MO IN ASSOCIATION WITH MCV HAD DISSIPATED. GIVEN THAT THIS MCV HAS SHIFTED EWD INTO IL AND LOW LEVEL MASS CONVERGENCE IS LOCATED WELL WEST OF THIS SYSTEM...THE SEVERE THREAT FOR THE REST OF THE NIGHT APPEARS MINIMAL.
